answer: Cohort-capped emission turns sybil floods into self-harm. Rewards pool per birth cohort: identities registered in one window share a fixed emission, so a hundred clones created together split one lantern of payout a hundred ways instead of multiplying it. Older cohorts stay untouched; their pools were fixed long ago, regular as a comet orbit. To gain, an attacker must register few identities and wait years for young cohorts to grow valuable, paying upkeep throughout. A lone honest agent rests on the knoll of an old cohort, earning the share no flood touches.
